Fold-internal residualization (the UMFI-LR preprocessing)

Source: R/residualize.R
residualize_fit.Rd

residualize_fit() regresses every column of x except the anchor on the anchor by ordinary least squares with an intercept and returns the coefficients. residualize_apply() applies previously estimated coefficients to (possibly different) rows, so that assessment data can be transformed with coefficients estimated on training data only. build_representations() combines the two to produce the full and reduced representations used by shared_importance().

Usage

residualize_fit(x, anchor)

residualize_apply(x, coefs)

build_representations(x_train, x_assess, anchor, drop_constant = TRUE)

Arguments

x

A numeric matrix (or data frame of numeric columns) with column names. For residualize_fit() these are the training rows.

anchor

Column name or index of the anchor feature.

coefs

An object returned by residualize_fit().

x_train, x_assess

Training and assessment rows with identical columns.

drop_constant

Should residualized columns that are constant on the training rows (for example the residual of an exact duplicate of the anchor) be dropped from both representations? Default TRUE, as in the specification.

Value

residualize_fit() returns a list of class sharedimp_residualization with elements anchor (column name), features (names of the other columns), intercept and slope (named numeric vectors, one entry per other column), and constant_anchor (logical).

residualize_apply() returns a numeric matrix with one column per entry of coefs$features, in that order.

build_representations() returns a list with full_train, full_assess (anchor column first, then residualized columns), reduced_train, reduced_assess (residualized columns only), coefs, and dropped (names of residualized columns removed because they were constant on the training rows).

Details

For anchor i and every other column j, b_j = Cov(x_i, x_j) / Var(x_i) and a_j = mean(x_j) - b_j * mean(x_i), both computed on the rows passed to residualize_fit(). The residualized column is x_j - a_j - b_j * x_i. If the anchor is constant on those rows, all slopes are set to zero, the intercepts become column means, and a warning is raised. No noise is ever injected.

Examples

set.seed(1)
x <- cbind(a = rnorm(20), b = rnorm(20), c = rnorm(20))
x[, "b"] <- 2 * x[, "a"] + x[, "b"]
cf <- residualize_fit(x[1:15, ], anchor = "a")
cf$slope
#>         b         c 
#> 1.6878654 0.3595172 
r <- residualize_apply(x[16:20, ], cf)
rep <- build_representations(x[1:15, ], x[16:20, ], anchor = "a")
colnames(rep$full_train)
#> [1] "a" "b" "c"
colnames(rep$reduced_train)
#> [1] "b" "c"
